auditMethod: I scored each ad against the §7 anchors only: 5 means a pleasant catalogue frame, and 9 means it matches the benchmarks (a half-second read at 200 px, a picture that proves the headline, verified size and offer). I applied the automatic caps literally, for example G9's five text blocks cap its message at 6. I held product-only frames with no skin or worn moment to 8.5 or below on desire. I measured scale in Feed px per listed mm against the 19 px/mm house rule: H2 about 17, S4 about 16.5, G9 about 17-19, Q2 about 19.5, V9 about 20, K7 about 25, Z2 about 34, G7 about 34, G4 about 39. All nine size lines are correct under that rule.

I scored each ad on its own against the §7 anchor text (5 = beige catalogue or two competing ideas, 9 = benchmark execution), using half points. I applied the automatic caps literally, counting the F2 card as one text element, which caps G9's one-message score at 6. I judged truth by measuring each piece's pixel extent in the Feed against its listed size. Results in px/mm: Q2 ≈19, K7 ≈25, V9 ≈19-20, S4 ≈16, G9 ≈18, G4 ≈38, G7 ≈34, Z2 ≈33, H2 ≈16.5. I then checked each ad's magnified line, or plain size, against the 19 px/mm house rule.

I scored each ad against the §7 absolute anchors (5 is beige or catalogue, 9 is benchmark) with the automatic caps applied, never against the other ads. I measured Feed px per listed mm on every piece. G9 (about 17), S4 (17) and H2 (17) sit under 19, so their plain size lines are right. V9 (20), Q2 (19.5), K7 (25), Z2 (about 30), G7 (34) and G4 (39) are at 19 or more, and each of them correctly carries "Shown magnified". I checked construction, counts and colour against the named reference photos. Compliance was checked against RULINGS §1 and §2: claims are allowed except on Pearl Double Halo and Monochrome, and stock and prices come from info.md.

I scored each ad on its own, against the §7 anchors (5 and 9) and automatic caps as amended by RULINGS.md, counting the F2 card as one text element. For scale I measured each piece's listed dimension in Feed pixels (halo, stone, hoop height or earring height, cross-checked against chain or wire gauge) and compared it with the 19 px/mm line: G4 about 39, G7 about 34, Z2 about 33, K7 about 25, V9 about 19.5 and Q2 about 19.2 all need and carry 'shown magnified'; H2 about 17, G9 about 17-18 and S4 about 16 are near life size and correctly carry a plain listed size.

blindMethod.t1: I opened only the one contact sheet and judged it at native thumbnail size, with no zoom. For each tile I asked two things. First, would the frame stop a 22-35 Indian woman scrolling, through colour contrast, product scale and sparkle? Second, is the first thing her eye lands on the jewellery itself, looking wanted, with a reason or price that comes across? Tiles where the product is large, high-contrast and backed by a short hook ranked top. Tiles where a prop, the dark background or text blocks land before the piece were marked down. I treated price as 'reads' when the rupee figure was legible on the sheet without enlarging, and the notes flag the marginal cases.
blindMethod.t2: I opened only the one sheet image and judged it at native thumbnail size, with no zoom or crop. For each tile I asked what the eye hits first in about half a second, whether the jewellery is the hero and looks desirable, and whether the price is legible. Tiles where a prop, a body or text won the first glance were marked down against tiles where the product itself landed first. The scores run from 3.5 to 8.5 so the ranking is visible.
blindMethod.t3: I read only the single contact sheet at thumbnail size, with no zoom or crop. I judged each tile on three things. First, what stops a 22-35 Indian woman's thumb in feed: contrast, colour and product scale in the frame. Second, whether the jewellery itself is the first thing the eye lands on and looks desirable. Third, whether the type of product, a rough size and the price read at feed size. Tiles that stop on a prop, food, text or empty dark backdrop were marked down even when they were attractive. The highest scores went to tiles where a large, clearly lit product and a readable price (ideally in the headline) work together. Same scale for every tile, whatever the brand or style.
blindMethod.t4: Opened only the single contact sheet (t4.png) with the Read tool and judged each 200x250 tile at sheet size, without zoom or crop. For each tile I asked what the eye hits first in about half a second, whether a 22-35-year-old Indian woman could tell what the item is and roughly how big it is, and whether a rupee figure is legible. Tiles where the jewellery itself is the first and largest focal point, with colour contrast and a covetable finish, ranked highest. Tiles that lead with a body, copy, labels or a multi-product grid were marked down, as were tiles where the product is small or low-contrast. Price legibility was a secondary tie-breaker: most tiles carry a small rupee figure, and only J9 puts it in the headline.
